Clinical glossary

CLINICAL REFERENCE

Definition index

Plain-language definitions for the measurements, stages, and model terminology used throughout the explorer.

INPUT VARIABLES

Clinical measurements

Each input is entered as a structured value for use by the model.

MAP mmHg
Mean arterial pressure: the average pressure driving blood through the systemic circulation during one cardiac cycle.
Cardiac index L/min/m²
Cardiac output adjusted for body surface area, describing how effectively the heart supplies systemic blood flow.
Lactate mmol/L
A metabolic marker that may rise when tissue oxygen delivery is inadequate or cellular metabolism is impaired.
SvO₂ %
Mixed venous oxygen saturation: the percentage of oxygen remaining in venous blood after systemic tissue extraction.
Urine output mL/kg/hr
Urine produced per kilogram of body weight per hour; reduced output can indicate impaired renal perfusion.
Neurological assessment
A categorized description of consciousness and responsiveness, ranging from alert and oriented to unresponsive.

STAGE REFERENCE

SCAI-like continuum

The explorer uses simplified A–E labels inspired by the SCAI framework.

A

At risk

Risk factors for cardiogenic shock without current shock signs.

B

Beginning

Relative hypotension or tachycardia without clear hypoperfusion.

C

Classic

A hypoperfusion pattern consistent with shock requiring intervention.

D

Deteriorating

Worsening pattern or failure to stabilize after initial support.

E

Extremis

Severe circulatory collapse or an equivalent near-arrest context.

MODEL LANGUAGE

Analytical terms

Raw ordinal score
The model's continuous numerical estimate before it is rounded and constrained to an A–E stage.
Coefficient (β)
A model weight describing the direction and relative contribution of an input to the calculated score.
Standardized variable
A numeric input transformed relative to its training-data mean and standard deviation before scoring.
Intercept
The starting value in the linear equation before the weighted input contributions are added.
Synthetic data
Artificially generated records designed to resemble plausible clinical patterns rather than observations from real patients.
SCAI-like stage
A simulated severity category inspired by the SCAI continuum; it is not a validated clinical classification.

DATA FORMAT

Structured and unstructured data

The five numeric measurements are structured data. Neurological assessment may begin as unstructured narrative documentation, but this dashboard converts it into a structured category so the model can process it consistently.
